market_specific_notes: USCIS grants what it calls a blanket designation to health departments: “We recognize all state and local health departments as civil surgeons, and they are authorized to complete the vaccination assessments for refugees seeking adjustment of status.” In Charleston that body is the Kanawha-Charleston Health Department. It covers the vaccination assessment for that category of applicant, not the full examination for everyone.

USCIS states plainly that “Many health insurance plans do not cover all portions of this examination”, and tells applicants to bring the insurance card and ask whether the civil surgeon accepts that plan for immigration medical examinations specifically. A plan that covers an annual physical is not evidence that it covers this.

Do not confuse the two places. The immigration medical examination is done by a civil surgeon in a private practice. The USCIS field office is where, in its own words, it holds “Interviews for all non-asylum cases (for example, getting a Green Card)” and “Naturalization ceremonies”. The 45 Charleston ZIP codes in the USCIS assignment file route to the Pittsburgh field office at Penn Center East, Building 7, 777 Penn Center Boulevard, Suite 600, Pittsburgh, PA 15235. That is across the state line from West Virginia. It surprises people, but it is routine: the assignment is federal, and a state border does not bound it. USCIS does not allow walk-ins at any field office; you must have an appointment.

West Virginia's reporting mandate covers children only: state law requires providers to report shots given to children under 18 to WVSIIS within two weeks. Adult doses are not compelled into the registry, so an adult applicant's WVSIIS record can be genuinely incomplete rather than merely missing. If the portal cannot match you, the state's fallback is to ask a provider or the local health department to print it from WVSIIS.

The Kanawha-Charleston Health Department is a genuinely combined city-county body: its six-member board is appointed three by the Kanawha County Commission and three by City of Charleston leadership. West Virginia's local public health is decentralised into 48 autonomous local boards of health and health departments.

The department performs skin tests at its Lee Street location on named weekdays, and hosts a free monthly diagnostic chest clinic staffed by a state tuberculosis physician — chest X-ray and physician review at no cost. It is monthly and by arrangement, not a walk-in service, so it fits a planned timeline and not an urgent one.

Work the checklist below in order. Verify designation in the federal locator first, and only then compare on travel, language and turnaround, because verification is the step that removes the most noise.
local_vetting_points: Search the official USCIS locator at uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon by the ZIP code you would actually travel to, not just “Charleston”.
Confirm the practice appears in that federal locator under the same name it bills and answers the phone under.
Use the locator's Languages Spoken filter before relying on a clinic's own marketing about language support.
Ask whether the examination, any laboratory work, any missing vaccines and the completed form happen on one visit or across several.
Ask what the office does on the day if a vaccination record turns out to be incomplete.
typical_cost_ranges: There is no published figure. USCIS: “Fees for immigration medical examinations are established by the civil surgeon. Fees may vary by civil surgeon.” Any site showing a Charleston rate is estimating, not reporting.

USCIS's own advice is to shop: “It may be helpful to call a few civil surgeons to find out how much they charge for the immigration medical examination. The cost of an immigration medical examination can vary significantly.”

When you call, ask each office to separate the examination, the tuberculosis and syphilis testing, any vaccines you are missing, completing and sealing the form, and any follow-up visit. Two quotes are comparable only once they cover the same list.
payment_options: USCIS instructs applicants to “check with the civil surgeon's office about acceptable forms of payment” before the visit. Ask on the call, not at the desk.
Bring the health insurance card and ask whether the office accepts that plan for immigration medical examinations specifically, since USCIS warns many plans do not cover all portions.
wait_time_notes: Two clocks run separately: how soon an office can see you, and how soon the completed form is ready. Ask about both, because an office can be quick on the first and slow on the second. Neither number is published anywhere, so the only way to get it is to ask.

USCIS says the civil surgeon tests for communicable diseases including tuberculosis and syphilis. A positive tuberculosis test adds a chest X-ray, and a missing vaccination record adds either repeat doses or blood work to prove immunity. Either turns one appointment into two.
availability_notes: Confirm whether a same-week appointment means the examination only, or the examination through to a completed, signed form.
If a filing deadline is close, name the date on the call and ask the office to commit or decline rather than leaving it open.

The Kanawha-Charleston Health Department — kchd.wv.gov. USCIS recognises state and local health departments as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment under its blanket designation.

USCIS Pittsburgh field office (PIT) — Penn Center East, Building 7, 777 Penn Center Boulevard, Suite 600, Pittsburgh, PA 15235. From the USCIS field office ZIP assignment data published at uscis.gov/about-us/find-a-uscis-office/field-offices.

the West Virginia Statewide Immunization Information System (WVSIIS) — oeps.wv.gov/immunizations. West Virginia says records “administered in West Virginia or otherwise documented in the West Virginia Immunization Information System (WVSIIS) can be accessed by patients or their parents directly using MyIR”. Public record request: myirmobile.com
the West Virginia Tuberculosis Elimination Program — oeps.wv.gov/tuberculosis-tb.

Listings are neutral examples and starting points for your own verification. Nothing here is a ranking or an endorsement.
city_intro_override: Charleston applicants should check one thing before anything else: the USCIS field office serving them is in another state. The local health department is a combined city-county body with real tuberculosis capacity, including a free monthly chest clinic staffed by a state physician — but the registry behind your vaccination record only compels reporting for children, so an adult record can be thin.

primary_city_decision_block.title: Local civil surgeon comparison checklist
items: Verify designation in the official USCIS locator before comparing anything else.
Ask for the cost broken into examination, labs, vaccines, form completion and follow-up.
Gather the vaccination records USCIS names before the first visit; WVSIIS is the route to your own record.
Ask what a positive tuberculosis test would do to the schedule and to what you are charged.
Tell the office whether the I-485 is going by mail or online, so the envelope is handled right.
Confirm the form edition and the date the civil surgeon intends to sign.

heading: Charleston: the field office is in Pittsburgh, and the registry only compels records for children
i693_document_requirements: Form I-693 itself, in the edition USCIS currently accepts. Confirm the edition with the office before the appointment.

Government-issued photo identification such as a valid passport or driver's licence. USCIS sets a different rule for applicants aged 14 or younger: identification showing name, date and place of birth and a parent's full name — a birth certificate with an English translation, or an affidavit.

A record of your vaccinations or immunisations. USCIS names the ones it means: DT, DTP, DTaP, Td, Tdap, OPV, IPV, MMR, Hib, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Varicella, Pneumococcal, Influenza, Rotavirus and Meningococcal disease.
Your health insurance card, with the question already prepared: does this office accept the plan for immigration medical examinations?
Payment, in a form the office has told you it accepts.
vaccination_handling_notes: Arriving with the records is the cheapest thing you can do. Without them the choice is repeat doses or blood tests to prove immunity, and both cost money and time.

In West Virginia the registry is the West Virginia Statewide Immunization Information System (WVSIIS), and it has a route for an individual to obtain their own record: West Virginia says records “administered in West Virginia or otherwise documented in the West Virginia Immunization Information System (WVSIIS) can be accessed by patients or their parents directly using MyIR”. Start at myirmobile.com and give yourself time before the appointment.

West Virginia's reporting mandate covers children only: state law requires providers to report shots given to children under 18 to WVSIIS within two weeks. Adult doses are not compelled into the registry, so an adult applicant's WVSIIS record can be genuinely incomplete rather than merely missing. If the portal cannot match you, the state's fallback is to ask a provider or the local health department to print it from WVSIIS.

If the record cannot be produced in time, the Kanawha-Charleston Health Department is a starting point, and the civil surgeon can order blood work to prove immunity instead. Ask which the office prefers before the visit rather than after it.

Refugees adjusting status may complete the vaccination assessment at a state or local health department under the USCIS blanket designation described above. That route is narrower than it sounds: it covers the vaccination assessment, not the whole examination, and only for that category.
bilingual_support: The official USCIS locator has a Languages Spoken filter with a long list of named languages. Use it. It is a federal field the practice itself filled in, which is a different thing from a claim on a clinic website.

The filter narrows the list; it does not promise that the paperwork review happens in that language. Ask specifically whether language support covers the form review, which is where a misunderstanding becomes a correction.
The same tool has a Doctor Sex filter, which matters to some applicants and is easy to miss.
appointment_booking_notes: Decide before the exam whether the I-485 is being filed by mail or online, because it changes what you do with the envelope. By mail it stays sealed. Online, USCIS instructs you to open it and upload the form, then keep the original and the envelope until the case is decided.
Ask the office which edition of Form I-693 it is completing and on what date it will sign. USCIS accepts only the 01/20/25 edition for forms signed on or after 3 July 2025.
Ask whether the slot you are offered is intake, the examination, or the full path through to a completed form.

Ask when the sealed packet is normally released, and what the correction process is if a signature or a date is wrong on it. Ask before choosing an office an hour away, because a correction may mean going back.
